issues.legal_issue: The limitation period for executing a final partition decree runs from the date the decree is passed, not the later date on which it is engrossed on stamp paper, unless the court has specifically postponed its enforceability.
material_facts: A final decree in a partition suit fixed the parties’ rights on 7 August 1981.
The decree holders supplied stamp papers on 25 May 1982, and the decree was engrossed thereafter; the court had not directed them to supply stamp papers.
The execution application was filed on 21 March 1994.
The lower courts treated the date of engrossment as the start of limitation.
issues.conclusion: The decree became enforceable when it was passed, and later engrossment related back to that date. The execution application was time-barred; the impugned judgment was set aside and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 136 of the Limitation Act, 1963 starts limitation when a decree becomes enforceable. Under Order 20 Rule 6A of the Code of Civil Procedure, a decree is generally enforceable from the pronouncement of judgment. In a partition suit, when the decree finally determines the parties’ rights, supplying stamp paper and engrossing the decree are ministerial acts; delay in those acts, which are within a party’s control, does not suspend limitation. Enforceability is postponed only where the court leaves an issue for later adjudication or specifically makes enforceability contingent on a later event. Sections 2(14), 2(15), 3, 33, 35, 40(b) and 42, and Article 45 of Schedule I of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 establish the fiscal treatment of partition decrees and the consequences of insufficient stamping; they do not suspend limitation under Article 136. The Court applied Hameed Joharan v. Abdul Salam, Renu Devi v. Mahendra Singh, and Yeshwant Deorao Deshmukh v. Walchand Ramchand Kothari; it treated the relevant observations in Shankar Balwant Lokhande v. Chandrakant Shankar Lokhande as obiter and the partition illustration in W.B. Essential Commodities Supply Corporation v. Swadesh Agro Farming & Storage as not an exposition of law. It also relied on Hindustan Steel Ltd. v. Dilip Construction Co. for the revenue-raising purpose of stamp legislation.

rule.if: partition_decree_execution and final_rights_fixed and not judicial_postponement and execution_outside_limitation_from_decree

predicates.partition_decree_execution: A party seeks execution of a final decree made in a partition proceeding.
predicates.final_rights_fixed: The court has finally determined the parties’ rights, leaving no matter for later adjudication.
predicates.judicial_postponement: The court has specifically made the decree’s enforceability contingent on a later event or postponed it to a later time.
predicates.execution_outside_limitation_from_decree: The execution application was filed after the applicable limitation period, counted from the date the decree was passed.

issues.definition: When execution is sought for a final partition decree whose enforceability the court has not postponed, an application filed outside the applicable limitation period counted from the decree date is time-barred.
